title: An opt-in MCP phase trace lets the next slow call name where its time went
outcome: An opt-in MCP phase trace lets the next slow call name where its time went
acceptance: Tests show stdout, results, errors and timeouts unchanged with the trace on; a writer-contention control raises begin_immediate; a blocked-client control keeps the server and send phases fast while the client's elapsed time rises; overflow, timeout and close stay bounded and visible; and one same-workload off/on comparison shows no measurable added work when the trace is off

The MCP dogfood runs with the opt-in, keeps the correlated records in its log, and prints a call's record beside its existing soft-threshold line when that call crosses it; a late, missing or evicted record is shown as unavailable, never as fast

With ENGRAM_MCP_PHASE_TRACE=1 at MCP server start, each tool call emits one bounded stderr record (at most 4 KiB) after it settles, correlated by the numeric request id, holding only the allowlisted phases handler_total, store_open_total, store_mutex_wait, begin_immediate, commit, receipt_serialize and wire_encode_send_inclusive, with no SQL, paths, parameters or bodies; unset, there are no hooks, buffers or output; while stderr is not drained, a record the bounded writer queue cannot take is dropped and counted in dropped_lines, never blocking the server

completion.summary: The opt-in MCP phase trace's acceptance gaps are closed. A slow call now gets its phase line immediately: either its record, or 'unavailable (record not yet received)' followed by the record when it arrives. A partial record (evicted, incomplete or cancelled) reads as unavailable, never as a fast call. A busy-timeout test shows that a traced and an untraced writer wait the same bound and are refused the same way, with the traced BEGIN IMMEDIATE showing the wait. The docs cover a wait that ends in the busy timeout. The carried failed evaluation 8026a47f ended through TermAl's --supersedes path, the first real use of that path; evaluation 330b2d24 passed 3/3.
